transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I keep trying to get rid of what I eat after I overdo it, and I feel like I can’t stop doing it on my own. It is so hard for me to admit this, but I feel completely stuck in this cycle and don't know what to do anymore.
When you try to get rid of what you ate, do you make yourself vomit or use laxatives, diuretics, or enemas?

I make myself throw up in the bathroom, and I turn the fan on so my husband won't hear me. I don't use laxatives, diuretics, or anything like that; I just force myself to vomit because I panic about the calories and desperately want to erase what I did, even though I feel so ashamed.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [F50.2, F50.8], but the patient now clearly reports recurrent self-induced vomiting after overeating, with intense fear of calories and shame. This strongly supports a specific eating disorder characterized by bingeing/purging behavior, while the more nonspecific residual category is no longer needed.

Compared with an initial broad differential, the pattern of loss of control and repeated self-induced removal of food makes the specific binge-purge syndrome more likely. A residual eating-disorder category remains possible because we do not yet know key details such as frequency, body image concerns, weight status, or whether the episodes meet full threshold criteria.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent self-induced vomiting after overeating, driven by intense fear of calories/weight-related consequences and a sense of loss of control over the behavior. This pattern is most consistent with bulimia nervosa, purging type (ICD-10 F50.2).
